Discussed success criteria (latency SLOs, cost per 1M tokens, quality thresholds), workload sizing (concurrency, qps, sequence lengths), streaming vs non-streaming tradeoffs, and security/KMS requirements. Agreed next steps to exchange harness repo, sample scripts, and schedule joint run next week.
transcript:
Header: 2025-12-03 14:00 UTC | Duration: 56m | Recording: enabled
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Reddy (NexaHealth - Platform Lead), Mark Dawson (NexaHealth - ML Eng), Eva Chen (NexaHealth - Security), Tom Alvarez (NexaHealth - SRE)

[00:00] Samir: Hey everybody, thanks for joining. Samir from Redwood, AE. We'll keep this to about 45-60 minutes, goal is to scope the POC bench and integration. Lena, do you want to intro the harness at a high level?
[00:22] Lena: Yeah, quick one. We have a lightweight benchmark harness that runs customer scripts against our serving endpoints. It supports streaming and non-streaming modes, configurable concurrency, and can run against Dedicated or Hosted. The harness is a small repo + docker runner. We'll send the link after.
[00:37] Priya: Awesome. For context, our main goals are to validate throughput for our chat assistant and make sure 95th pct latency is under 600ms for 1:1 conversations. Cost is important but latency first.
[00:49] Mark: We're planning two workloads: a short-chat workload (avg 40 tokens outbound, 30 tokens inbound) at 120 QPS and a long-context summarization workload (avg 800 tokens) at low concurrency (~2-5 qps). We want to see both.
[01:10] Tom: SRE cares about cold start behavior and KV cache warmup times, also autoscaling behavior during spike to 300 QPS for short bursts.
[01:22] Eva: Security: we need to confirm KMS integration, audit logs, and whether any customer data persists on Redwood logs. SOC2 and ISO evidence required for procurement.
[01:37] Samir: Great — all standard. Quick question on success criteria: Priya mentioned 95th pct < 600ms for short-chat, is there a cost target you want to tie to that?
[01:51] Priya: Ideally we want cost per 1M tokens to be competitive with our current (internal) infra -- ballpark $40-$60 per 1M tokens, but again latency more important for now. We'll use cost as a tiebreaker.
[02:06] Lena: Ok, so for the harness we'll capture latency distributions, token accounting, per-request payload sizes, and a trace that maps to the Redwood console. We'll also export results as CSV so you can plug into your dashboards.
[02:20] Mark: Important: our current client uses streaming websocket calls for user-facing chat. We need to test both streaming and batch (non-streaming) to see differences. The streaming path is critical for UX.
[02:33] Lena: Our runtime supports streaming with incremental tokens and we can reproduce streaming semantics. Two caveats: streaming adds overhead per-connection and long-lived connections change autoscaling dynamics; for throughput-focused tests we also do non-streaming with chunked batch sends.
[02:49] Priya: Can you simulate slow clients? We have mobile clients that add latency; we want to ensure p95 under 600ms in normal network conditions, not ideal.
[02:59] Lena: Yes, harness can inject client-side latency and jitter. We'll include a mobile profile.

--- Topics: success criteria, harness repo, sample scripts, security docs, timeline ---

[03:20] Samir: Let's go through workload sizing specifics. Mark, can you confirm expected concurrency distributions?
[03:27] Mark: For chat: sustained 120 QPS from global frontends, with 1.2 tokens per outbound message on avg? sorry outbound tokens were 40, inbound 30, so total ~70 tokens per round trip. Peak bursts may hit 300 QPS for 30s. For summarization: 2-5 QPS but heavy token count.
[03:50] Samir: Good. For benchmarking we usually run a mix: a steady 15-minute ramp to steady-state then 3 spike windows (30s each) to test autoscaling. We'll need to coordinate when you can run traffic through your prod-like environment vs a test VPC.
[04:05] Priya: We'll run in a staging VPC that's network-equivalent. We need to know firewall rules and IP allowlist for the harness runner.
[04:15] Lena: We'll provide the runner IP ranges and a docker image if you want to host it in your VPC. You can also run from a proxy host in our cloud. We'll share the exact instructions in the repo.
[04:28] Tom: On orchestration - does the harness open thousands of socket connections for streaming? Concerned about ephemeral ports.
[04:36] Lena: It can, yes. We recommend using our runner with connection pooling, and we can throttle connections per host. For streaming tests we'll use connection reuse to approximate real client behavior.

[05:00] Mark: For quantization and model variants: we may want to test a 4-bit quantized variant vs fp16. Will your runtime surface perf/cost differences?
[05:10] Samir: Absolutely. We can run the same model in different quantization profiles. Redwood has model variants and we'll log tokens/sec, latency, and cost per token for each. Note that quantization may slightly affect quality; you'll want evaluation prompts too.
[05:24] Mark: We'll include a quality sample set of ~500 prompts to run against each variant and measure agreement with baseline.
[05:31] Priya: Can the harness compute quality/regression metrics or do we feed outputs back to our eval infra?
[05:38] Lena: The harness will compute basic n-gram overlap and BLEU-like metrics, but for domain-specific evaluation you'll feed outputs into your eval pipeline. We'll return raw outputs and timestamps.

[05:55] Eva: On encryption: we require CMEK and HSM-backed KMS for keys. Also audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. Is that available in Redwood Private/Dedicated?
[06:06] Samir: Yes — Dedicated and Private have CMEK options and HSM integrations; Hosted can do customer-managed keys in select regions. We'll send the security pack with SOC2/ISO artifacts. For logs we can stream audit logs to your S3 or syslog collector.
[06:21] Eva: Great, please include retention settings and how long artifacts are kept by default.

[06:33] Lena: Back to harness integration: typical flow is Mark/engineer drops in their inference script (we support both Python requests and websocket examples). The harness wraps your script to emit metrics and do warmup, then runs the test profiles. We have example configs: short-chat-streaming.json, short-chat-batch.json, long-summarize.json.
[06:56] Mark: Awesome. We'll take the short-chat-streaming and run it with our message patterns. Does the harness support per-request variable sequence length?
[07:04] Lena: Yes, you can supply distributions for sequence length or point estimates. We commonly support histograms so your real distribution is approximated.

[07:20] Priya: Timeline question: how long to get meaningful numbers? We expect to run a 2-week POC, with first week integration and initial runs, second week focused on repeated runs and fine-tuning. Can you support that?
[07:34] Samir: That's standard — 2-week POC is good. Week 1: repo, sample scripts, one joint run. Week 2: run variations, compare variants, and finalize success criteria. We'll provide a suggested plan in the follow-up email.
[07:47] Tom: Who owns cost for Dedicated infra during POC? We assume Redwood provides a short-term eval environment.
[07:55] Samir: For POC we typically provide a limited Public/Hosted trial with capacity. If you want Dedicated instances reserved for a POC we'll discuss credits or a short-term commitment; I'll include options in pricing.

[08:12] Mark: For telemetry, what tracing hooks do you expose so we can correlate requests from our frontends to Redwood spans?
[08:20] Lena: We can add trace ids in headers and export traces to Jaeger/Zipkin. We also have per-request metadata you can set to match your request ids.

[08:33] Priya: One more: do you have any pre-built connectors for our stack (we use internal envoy + k8s + GCP)?
[08:41] Samir: No vendor-specific connector required; the harness runs as a pod or docker container behind your network. We'll provide example k8s manifests for running the runner as a Job or Deployment.

[09:00] Mark: Let's outline the exact metrics we want from the benchmark: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, token cost, error rates, connection churn, and quality metrics per variant.
[09:12] Lena: We'll ensure the harness emits those. Also suggest we capture KV cache hit-rate and warmup time as a separate metric for long-context flows.
[09:22] Samir: Regarding streaming vs non-streaming: streaming gives better perceived latency but may increase p95 due to incremental round trips if the model stalls. We should run both and compare end-to-end perceived latency (time to first token) and completion latency.
[09:38] Tom: For autoscale testing, what's your suggestion for load pattern? We want to see how scaling behaves at 120 qps sustained with 3x spike.
[09:47] Lena: We'll run a ramp: 5 minutes ramp to 120 qps, 20 minutes steady, then 3 spike events with 30s at 300 qps, and let autoscaler settle. We'll record pod counts and latency curves.

[10:05] Priya: Any gotchas?
[10:08] Lena: Watch out for client-side connection limits and ephemeral port exhaustion when running streaming at high concurrency. Also, network throttling in your staging env can mask performance. We recommend a runner inside the same region.
[10:22] Mark: For the sample scripts, we'll provide two artifacts tonight: a streaming websocket runner and a synchronous REST runner. Expect ~10k lines? I mean 10k prompts across the test set; sorry.
[10:34] Samir: Perfect. After you share we'll do a smoke test and then a full run. We'll try to schedule the joint run Thurs or Fri next week.

[10:50] Eva: On audit and procurement, we'll need SOC2 Type II plus Pen test summary. We'll also need a data flow diagram for the POC.
[10:59] Samir: I'll attach the security pack and a one-page POC data flow diagram in the follow-up.

[11:10] Priya: Can we capture an expected report template so procurement can review quickly?
[11:16] Samir: Yes, we'll include a POC report template with the metrics and pass/fail criteria.

[11:30] Mark: Quick note: for quality threshold we expect >95% parity on the 500 prompt eval set vs our baseline for the short-chat. If quantized model drops below, we consider that regression.
[11:45] Lena: We'll run the eval set and provide diff outputs so your eval infra can calculate exact parity.

--- Recap & Next Steps ---
[12:00] Samir: Recap: 2-week POC, harness repo share (Lena), Nexus to provide sample scripts and 500 prompt eval set (Mark), security docs and KMS requirements (Eva), Samir to send pricing and POC capacity options. Schedule joint harness run next week.
[12:20] Priya: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[12:24] Samir: Thanks — we'll follow up with links and a proposed schedule.
[12:30] Meeting ended.
